alternatives.reason: Modelling all of GCS's tiered egress destinations, all storage classes, retrieval fees, operation-class pricing and free-tier thresholds is a full billing engine, not a P0 minimal slice. It also needs inputs (retention period, destination mix, storage class) the Change Request does not collect today, which would force the calculator to guess them. Deferred until a real business_constraints field exists for each input.

vision.md's own requirement is that GeminiAdvisor names cost drivers in words while a deterministic function does the arithmetic. An LLM-produced dollar figure is not reproducible (same input can yield a different number on a different call) and cannot be traced to a source_url/as_of the way a price-table lookup can. Both RuleAdvisor and GeminiAdvisor candidates are priced by the same EstimateOptionCost function; the advisor never emits an amount.

managed_storage_with_signed_urls names three drivers in prose: stored bytes over retention, download egress, metadata reads/writes. Only download egress is priced in this slice, because expected_monthly_volume (the one business constraint the Change Request collects) most naturally reads as a transfer/traffic volume, not a retention-scoped storage size. Pricing 'stored bytes' would require a retention-period input that does not exist yet; pricing metadata ops would require a request-count input and an Class A/B operations SKU that has not been sourced. Both stay UNKNOWN line items with an explicit reason rather than being inferred from the same volume number.

The price table is a Go source map (pricing.go) with a version string, not a database row or admin UI. Changing a price requires a code change and a price_table_version bump, which keeps every past CostEstimate traceable to the exact table that produced it. An editable table is future scope once more SKUs are added.

architecture_impact: Option (internal/change/model.go) gains CostEstimate: a structured field with status ESTIMATED|UNKNOWN, monthly_low/base/high, a per-driver Breakdown ([]CostLineItem, each traceable to sku/currency/unit/region/source_url/as_of when ESTIMATED), Assumptions, PriceTableVersion and ParsedVolumeGiB. CostDrivers ([]string, the advisor's prose) is unchanged and kept alongside it.

internal/change/pricing.go adds a versioned PriceTable (PriceTableVersion = gcp-pricing-2026-09-27): two PriceRecord entries (gcs-standard-storage, gcs-network-egress-worldwide-tier1), each carrying unit_price/unit/currency/region/source_url/as_of/known. A price with known=false can never produce an amount.

internal/change/calculator.go adds EstimateOptionCost(optionID, business_constraints) — pure, deterministic, no LLM/clock/network call. It looks up expected_monthly_volume, parses it with ParseMonthlyVolumeGiB (GB/MB/TB read as the JEDEC-binary GiB/MiB/TiB GCS itself bills in; anything that does not match a leading number + GB-family unit token is UNKNOWN, never guessed), and for managed_storage_with_signed_urls prices the download-egress line item at low/base/high = parsed_gib * {0.5, 1.0, 2.0} * unit_price. LowScenarioMultiplier/BaseScenarioMultiplier/HighScenarioMultiplier are named constants documenting that the spread models input uncertainty in the one supplied volume number, not measured usage variance (P0 has no historical volume data). Every other option ID has no priced SKU mapped to it and is UNKNOWN by construction (costableOptions allow-list).

internal/change/service.go's evaluateVersion runs EstimateOptionCost over every option after the advisor (RuleAdvisor or GeminiAdvisor) returns, so CostEstimate always reflects the calculator regardless of which advisor proposed the candidate. DecisionRecord.Alternatives copies Options by value, so the estimate flows into the DecisionRecord and Brief unchanged.
frontend/src/api/changes.ts adds CostLineItem/CostEstimate types and an optional Option.cost_estimate (absent on records rendered before the calculator existed, so no fixture is invalidated).

frontend/src/components/ChangesPanel.tsx adds CostEstimateLine, rendered under each option's existing cost/risks line in DecisionForm: renders 'est. {low} / {base} / {high} {currency} per month (low/base/high)' when ESTIMATED, or 'cost estimate: UNKNOWN — {reason}' when UNKNOWN. The component only copies values already computed by the backend; it adds no fact and does not compute or round beyond formatMoney's toFixed(2) cosmetic pass. New keys added to frontend/src/i18n/zh-TW.ts messages; the amounts and reason string are data values and are not translated.

Review feedback ('needs minor fixes', 2026-09-27): an ESTIMATED line sitting directly under all three named cost drivers read as if it summed all three, and it did not say which GCP region the price came from. CostEstimate gains Region (the short origin region a priced line item was queried against, e.g. 'us-central1') and CoveredDrivers/UnpricedDrivers (calculator.go derives both from Breakdown's own per-item Status right after building it — never decided independently, so they cannot disagree with Breakdown). PriceRecord gains OriginRegion alongside the existing descriptive Region field. CostEstimateLine now renders a second line, 'covers: {covered} · excludes (UNKNOWN): {excluded} · {region} pricing', directly under the amount line, only when ESTIMATED (data-testid=cost-estimate-scope); zh-TW gets a matching key, translating only the surrounding words.

William's decision (2026-09-27): Gemini candidates must also be priceable, in this same slice. Option gains PricingRef (json pricing_ref, model.go); EstimateOptionCost(optionID, pricingRef, business_constraints) now takes pricingRef and uses it when non-empty in place of optionID against costableOptions — an empty, 'none' or unrecognised pricing_ref is UNKNOWN with a reason naming the value, never a fuzzy match; an empty pricing_ref (the RuleAdvisor path — it never sets the field) falls through to the original optionID-based match unchanged. GeminiAdvisor (advisor.go) generates the allowed pricing_ref list from costableOptions itself via pricingRefChoices() (never a hand-duplicated list in the prompt), states that same list in the prompt text, and now also sends a Gemini responseSchema (previously not used at all) with pricing_ref typed as an enum over that list, calling for id/title/summary/pricing_ref as required. The schema and prompt only narrow what a well-behaved model returns; EstimateOptionCost's own validation is the actual enforcement and does not trust either. ChangesPanel.tsx and both locale files are unchanged — no UI string yet shows pricing_ref or which advisor/ref an ESTIMATED amount was actually priced through; the existing scope-disclosure line already names the covered/unpriced drivers and region regardless of which advisor proposed the option, which was judged sufficient for this pass.
cost_assumptions: Prices are USD, region us-central1 (storage) / origin us-central1 destination worldwide excluding Asia & Australia (egress), queried live from https://cloud.google.com/storage/pricing on 2026-09-27 — the page shows no visible last-updated date, so as_of records the query date, not a page revision date.

gcs-standard-storage: 0.02 USD per GiB-month, derived from the page's per-GiB-hour figure (0.000027397) for the Iowa (us-central1) region selector times 730 average hours/month; cross-checked against the well-known public $0.02/GiB-month figure for Standard storage in that region. This SKU is recorded in the price table but is NOT used by EstimateOptionCost in this slice (see rejected alternative: stored bytes stays UNKNOWN because retention period is not collected).

gcs-network-egress-worldwide-tier1: 0.12 USD per GiB, taken from the page's 'General network usage' table, first cumulative-volume tier (0-10 TiB/month), origin us-central1 to worldwide destinations excluding Asia & Australia and China. EstimateOptionCost always uses this single tier and does not model higher-volume tier breakpoints; a monthly volume large enough to cross into a cheaper tier will still be priced entirely at the tier-1 rate, which is a conservative (over-, not under-) estimate.

LowScenarioMultiplier = 0.5, BaseScenarioMultiplier = 1.0, HighScenarioMultiplier = 2.0 applied to parsed_volume_gib * unit_price: base is the number as declared; low/high are a +-2x band around it to represent that a single self-reported traffic estimate is uncertain, not a statistically derived confidence interval.

Region mismatch, explicitly disclosed rather than fixed: every priced entry in the table is queried for us-central1. The 10/6 Cloud Run deploy runbook (docs/operations/CLOUD_RUN_DEPLOY_2026-10-06.zh-TW.md:21, already on develop) records the deploy region default as asia-east1 (scripts/deploy-cloud-run.sh:31, cloudbuild.yaml:12, scripts/bootstrap-w1.sh:19). GCS Standard storage and network-egress unit prices for asia-east1 were not looked up for this slice — a WebFetch/curl pass to confirm them was out of scope for a 'needs minor fixes' pass — so the price table keeps us-central1 rather than guessing an asia-east1 number; CostEstimate.region names us-central1 explicitly (surfaced in the UI as '{region} pricing') so a reader is not left to assume the estimate matches wherever the service actually deploys. Re-querying both SKUs for asia-east1 and bumping price_table_version is future work if the deploy region stays asia-east1.
unknowns: Only 2 of the 3 cost drivers vision.md and the RuleAdvisor name for managed_storage_with_signed_urls are priced: download egress is ESTIMATED, 'stored bytes over retention' and 'metadata reads/writes' are UNKNOWN line items with an explicit reason (no retention-period business constraint exists; no metadata operations SKU has been sourced). The option's CostEstimate.monthly_* therefore understates the option's true total cost and must not be read as full TCO.

Only 2 SKUs are in the price table; every option other than managed_storage_with_signed_urls (including every option a GeminiAdvisor might propose with a different id) has no priced SKU mapped to it and reports CostEstimate.status = UNKNOWN with reason 'no priced SKU is mapped to option ...'. Extending pricing to more options is future work, not a gap in this slice's own scope.

The egress tier is fixed at the first cumulative-volume tier (0-10 TiB/month); a genuinely large expected_monthly_volume would in real billing move into a cheaper per-GiB tier that this calculator does not model, so very large estimates are conservatively high, never low.

DR-013 exists on another branch and was not visible from this worktree; DR-012 was used as the sole structural template. If DR-013 introduced schema changes to the DR-NNN format, this record may need reconciling once branches merge.

The volume parser accepts a small fixed set of unit spellings (gib/gb/tib/tb/mib/mb, case-insensitive, optional thousands separators, optional trailing '/month' or 'per month'); any other phrasing (e.g. '500 requests', a bare number with no unit, or a unit token before the number) is treated as unparseable and the whole CostEstimate is UNKNOWN, per the 'never guess' requirement.

GeminiAdvisor candidates are never priced by SKU, structurally, not just today: advisor.go:206 rewrites every Gemini-proposed option's ID to gemini_option_N (N = index+1) before it reaches the calculator, and costableOptions only matches the literal id managed_storage_with_signed_urls. So even if a future Gemini candidate is conceptually the same managed-storage option, its rewritten id makes EstimateOptionCost report UNKNOWN with 'no priced SKU is mapped to option gemini_option_N'. Matching on option content instead of a fixed id is future work.（2026-09-27 更新：William 裁決 Gemini 方案也要能定價，已在同分支追加處理，見下方新增的 unknowns 項目。Option 新增 PricingRef 欄位，GeminiAdvisor 的 prompt 與 responseSchema（新加）共同約束每個 option 必須帶 pricing_ref，值只能是 costableOptions 的 key 或 "none"，由 pricingRefChoices() 從 costableOptions 產生、不在 prompt 裡手寫重複清單。EstimateOptionCost 優先讀 pricing_ref：空值、"none"、或不在清單內一律 UNKNOWN 並附原因（例如 pricing_ref "xyz" is not a priced SKU），不做模糊比對。RuleAdvisor 從不設定 pricing_ref，其路徑退回原本以 optionID 比對 costableOptions 的行為，未受影響。測試見 tests/change/advisor_test.go（httptest fake Gemini server：合法 pricing_ref→ESTIMATED、非法值→UNKNOWN 附原因、缺欄位→UNKNOWN）與 tests/change/calculator_test.go 新增的三個 pricing_ref 優先權/驗證測試。）

The real-run demo fixture (evidence/EB-012/chg-001-candidate.json, CHG-001) sets expected_monthly_volume to the literal string '200 references per month'. 'references' is not a GB-family unit token the parser recognizes, so ParseMonthlyVolumeGiB treats it as unparseable and the option's CostEstimate.status renders UNKNOWN in the demo, not ESTIMATED — this is the calculator behaving correctly (a business-object count is not a byte volume), not a bug. No references-to-GiB conversion factor is invented here to make the demo show an amount; evidence/ and the demo fixture/state are forbidden paths for this DR and are left untouched. How (or whether) to give the demo a GB-family volume so it can show ESTIMATED is left to William.

Real Gemini schema/enum compliance is UNVERIFIED: this workspace has no GEMINI_API_KEY and no egress to generativelanguage.googleapis.com, so geminiResponseSchema's pricing_ref enum and the matching prompt wording have only been exercised against a fake httptest server that returns exactly the JSON each test supplies (advisor_test.go) — never against a real model that might ignore the schema, wrap pricing_ref in extra text, or omit it under load. EstimateOptionCost's own validation (pricing_ref must be a literal costableOptions key or it is UNKNOWN with a reason) is the actual enforcement and does not depend on the real Gemini API honouring the schema, but whether real Gemini responses typically comply — and how often the schema-violation UNKNOWN path fires in practice — stays unverified until a run with a real key is recorded as evidence, expected after the 10/6 Cloud Run deploy.

pricing_ref is only checked for membership in costableOptions, never for whether it actually matches the candidate's own content: EstimateOptionCost has no way to tell that a pricing_ref naming a real SKU was attached to a conceptually unrelated option. For example, a Gemini candidate proposing a Firestore-based design could still carry pricing_ref "managed_storage_with_signed_urls" (the GCS egress SKU) — a value on the allowed list, so it passes validation and prices the Firestore option using GCS egress pricing, silently wrong rather than UNKNOWN. costableOptions has exactly one entry today, so the chance of this in practice is low, but it is a real, undisclosed gap, not something the current code guards against; a content-vs-SKU consistency check (e.g. matching against the option's own cost_drivers wording, or a per-SKU keyword allow-list) is future work once more SKUs exist and this stops being a one-entry coincidence.
acceptance_criteria: EstimateOptionCost is deterministic: identical optionID + business_constraints always produce a reflect.DeepEqual-identical CostEstimate (TestEstimateOptionCostIsDeterministic).

An option with no priced SKU mapped to it, a missing expected_monthly_volume constraint, or a volume string the parser cannot read all produce status UNKNOWN with a non-empty reason and zero invented amounts (TestEstimateOptionCostUnknownOptionHasNoSKU, TestEstimateOptionCostMissingBusinessConstraintIsUnknown, TestEstimateOptionCostUnparseableVolumeIsUnknown).

A parseable volume on the one priced option produces low < base < high with low/base/high = parsed_gib * {0.5,1.0,2.0} * unit_price, and every ESTIMATED line item carries sku/currency/region/source_url/as_of and at least one recorded assumption (TestEstimateOptionCostScenarioArithmetic, TestEstimateOptionCostTraceability).

If a price_table entry is marked unknown (Known=false), the estimate that depends on it falls back to UNKNOWN rather than using a stale or invented number (TestEstimateOptionCostUnknownPriceProducesUnknownLine).

Every option recorded on every ChangeVersion (both RuleAdvisor and GeminiAdvisor candidates) carries a CostEstimate produced by EstimateOptionCost, verified at the service layer, not only at the calculator's own unit-test layer (TestOptionsCarryDeterministicCostEstimates, and the extended TestSupplyingInputsCreatesNewVersionAndBecomesReady).

The workspace shows the low/base/high line for an ESTIMATED option and the reason for an UNKNOWN option, with the ESTIMATED amounts appearing unchanged (only surrounding wording translated) in both en and zh-TW locales (frontend/tests/components/changesPanel.test.tsx cost-estimate-known / cost-estimate-unknown cases).

A Gemini candidate carrying a valid pricing_ref is priced via EstimateOptionCost exactly as a RuleAdvisor candidate with the same underlying SKU would be, regardless of its own (possibly rewritten) id; an invalid, "none", or missing pricing_ref is UNKNOWN with a reason, never a fuzzy match; and pricing_ref always takes priority over optionID when set (TestGeminiAdvisorPricingRefEstimated, TestGeminiAdvisorInvalidPricingRefIsUnknown, TestGeminiAdvisorMissingPricingRefIsUnknown, TestEstimateOptionCostPricingRefTakesPriorityOverOptionID, TestEstimateOptionCostInvalidPricingRefIsUnknown, TestEstimateOptionCostNonePricingRefIsUnknown).
